small_guidance:
- The conv now dominates runtime (instance_norm+div is fused and fast). Add a vectorized 2-pass with larger BLOCK (e.g., 65536) only marginally helps; the main lever is replacing nn.Conv2d. For the existing norm kernel, try BLOCK=16384 num_warps=4 num_stages=4 to reduce register pressure on the H*W=15876 case.
- Consider fusing the conv bias add directly into the instance_norm kernel's first pass (skip materializing bias-added intermediate) once conv is custom.
- Use float4 vectorized loads (tl.load with 4-wide) on contiguous HW to improve memory bandwidth in the norm kernel.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.Conv2d with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel: program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit im2col gather, BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32 starting point, channels_last layout so IC is the GEMM-K contiguous axis. Conv output is 128×128×126×126 with K=64·3·3=576 — well-suited to a tiled GEMM.
- Fuse the conv epilogue with instance-norm: write conv output to global, then a second persistent kernel per (N,C) computes mean/var and applies (x-mean)*rstd/divide_by in one pass. Alternatively, do a Welford accumulation inside the conv kernel's per-(N,C) tile if the OC tile aligns to a full channel.
- Fold the conv bias into the GEMM epilogue and pre-scale weight by 1/divide_by only if it remains post-norm — actually fold 1/divide_by into the rstd scale (already done). Keep conv bias add in the conv kernel epilogue to avoid an extra pass.
